name: Anteromedial approach to the distal tibia
corridor: Immediately medial to the intact tibialis-anterior tendon sheath with sagittal capsulotomy between anterior articular fragments

positioning.text: Position supine on a radiolucent table with free ankle motion and access for orthogonal imaging and tibial-to-talar distraction.

setup.text: Delay definitive fixation until soft-tissue recovery is appropriate, map fragments on CT, preserve planned skin bridges, and plan medial/anterior plating before incision.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark tibial crest, tibialis-anterior tendon, ankle joint, medial malleolus, navicular base, and any traumatic wounds or prior incisions.

incision.text: Begin 5-8 cm proximal to joint just lateral to tibial crest and continue straight toward navicular base along the medial border of tibialis-anterior tendon.

superficial_interval.text: Raise a full-thickness flap without undermining adjacent skin bridges and expose the medial edge of the tibialis-anterior tendon sheath without opening it.

deep_interval.text: Incise periosteum just medial to the intact tendon sheath, develop the plane behind the sheath laterally only as needed, and open joint sagittally along the fracture interval.

layers.text: Skin, full-thickness anteromedial flap, periosteum medial to tibialis-anterior sheath, sagittal capsule, then medial/central plafond.

structures_encountered.text: Tibialis-anterior tendon sheath, anterior capsule, anteromedial and anterolateral articular fragments, medial malleolus, and talar dome are encountered.

structures_at_risk.text: Anteromedial skin flap, tibialis-anterior tendon and sheath, saphenous nerve/vein medially, anterior tibial vessels, fragment blood supply, and talar cartilage are at risk.

danger_zones.text: Do not violate the tibialis-anterior tendon sheath; repair any traumatic or inadvertent opening immediately to prevent tendon exposure beneath the wound.

retraction_hazards.text: Avoid undermining the medial flap, forceful tendon retraction, or broad transverse capsular release that devascularizes anterior fragments.

exposure.text: Provides excellent medial and central plafond and medial-malleolar visualization with access to central/posterior impaction through fragment mobilization.

limitations.text: The far anterolateral Chaput fragment may require a separate small anterolateral window, and the medial soft-tissue envelope is vulnerable.

extensions.text: Extend proximally along tibial crest or add a separate limited anterolateral incision when direct lateral fixation cannot be performed safely through this corridor.

indications.text: Use for medial/central plafond injuries, medial-malleolar involvement, and varus patterns with medial comminution or buttress requirements.

relative_contraindications.text: Prefer an anterolateral or posterior corridor when medial skin is traumatized or dominant fracture fragments cannot be accessed without excessive stripping.

implant_implications.text: Supports medial or anterior plates and distal-to-proximal submuscular bridging; use a separate lateral window when screw trajectory requires it.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Use AP, lateral, mortise, and oblique views to verify joint congruity, restored alignment, talar centering, and extra-articular implant placement.

closure.text: Close sagittal capsule and periosteum, confirm the tibialis-anterior sheath is intact, and approximate viable full-thickness skin without tension.

complications.text: Complications include wound-edge necrosis, infection, tibialis-anterior exposure or adhesions, saphenous neuropathy, malreduction, nonunion, stiffness, and post-traumatic arthritis.

bailouts.text: Use a separate limited anterolateral window for an inaccessible Chaput fragment rather than extending beneath a tenuous skin bridge or tendon sheath.

procedure_applications.condition: Medial and central plafond injury, medial-malleolar involvement, or varus-associated medial comminution requires direct access

questions.question: Which tendon sheath must remain intact?
Where is the preferred capsulotomy?
questions.answer: Sagittal, usually along the fracture interval between the main anterior fragments.

questions.question: Which pattern particularly favors this approach?
questions.answer: Varus pilon injury with medial comminution or medial-malleolar involvement.
